subject: psychiatry
title: Psychological testing: intelligence, cognition and personality assessment

steps.tx: Psychological testing measures **intelligence**, cognition and personality in a standard way. The intelligence quotient compares a person's performance with the average for age. The WHO classifies mental retardation by IQ: mild 50 to 70, moderate 35 to 49, severe 20 to 34, and profound below 20. A child with an IQ below 70 is considered to have intellectual impairment.
steps.say: Psychological testing measures intelligence, cognition and personality in a standard way. The intelligence quotient compares a person's performance with the average for age. The WHO classifies mental retardation by IQ: mild fifty to seventy, moderate thirty-five to forty-nine, severe twenty to thirty-four, and profound below twenty. A child with an IQ below seventy is considered to have intellectual impairment.

steps.tx: Indian textbooks classify **intelligence quotient** scores in finer bands. A score of 90 to 109 falls in the **normal** range, 110 to 119 is **superior**, and 120 to 139 is **very superior**. Scores of 140 and above are termed **near genius**. Learn these labels as a set, because examiners often ask you to match a given score to its band.
steps.say: Indian textbooks classify intelligence quotient scores in finer bands. A score of ninety to one hundred and nine falls in the normal range, one hundred and ten to one hundred and nineteen is superior, and one hundred and twenty to one hundred and thirty-nine is very superior. Scores of one hundred and forty and above are termed near genius. Learn these labels as a set, because examiners often ask you to match a given score to its band.

steps.tx: The **Wechsler** scales are the most widely used intelligence tests. The adult version, WAIS, is centred on an IQ of 100 with a standard deviation of 15, so about 68 percent of adults score between 85 and 115. Wechsler bands call 90 to 109 average and 70 to 79 borderline. The Stanford-Binet scale suits children aged 2 to 18 years for general intellectual ability.
steps.say: The Wechsler scales are the most widely used intelligence tests. The adult version, WAIS, is centred on an IQ of one hundred with a standard deviation of fifteen, so about sixty-eight percent of adults score between eighty-five and one hundred and fifteen. Wechsler bands call ninety to one hundred and nine average and seventy to seventy-nine borderline. The Stanford-Binet scale suits children aged two to eighteen for general intellectual ability.

steps.tx: Bender Gestalt test asks the patient to copy designs and is the best screen for **organic brain damage**. Projective tests such as the Rorschach inkblot test, Thematic Apperception Test and sentence completion test assess personality through open responses. The Rorschach uses 10 inkblots and helps separate psychotic from non-psychotic thinking. Halstead-Reitan is a neuropsychological battery for general cognition.
